newsitem.title: USA: US House lawmakers to speed up cereal price report.
newsitem.headline: US House lawmakers to speed up cereal price report.

text.p: A pair of House lawmakers have responded to a major breakfast cereal maker's decision to boost prices by accelerating plans to release their annual report on the industry's pricing practices.
On Wednesday, General Mills Corp, the M.S.'s second largest cereal maker, said it was raising its cereal prices by an average of 2.6 percent, effective immediately.
The move made General Mills the first major cereal maker to boost prices since a round of industry cuts last year.
General Mills said it took the action to adjust for inflation.

But Rep. Sam Gejdenson, a Connecticut Democrat, on Thursday accused the company of "playing games with consumers." "Their 11 percent price reduction, announced last June, applied to less than half of their cereal products," Gedjenson said in a statement. It also excluded Cheerios and Wheaties, two of their best-selling plans, he said.

The General Mills price hike is not likely to prompt legislation, but it has accelerated plans by Gedjenson and Rep. Charles Schumer, a New York Democrat, to release their third annual report on cereal industry pricing practices.

Gedjenson has been on a crusade against what he regards as excessively high cereal prices since 1994, when he noticed on a shopping trip with his children that some cereal was priced at close to $5.00 a box, an aide said.
Shortly after the second Gedjenson-Schumer report last year, Post Cereal cut its cereal prices by 20 percent.
That action by Post, a division of Philip Morris Cos Inc's Krafts Foods Inc unit, prompted General Mills, Kellogg Co and Quaker Oats Co also to cut prices.

The thrust of the third Gedjenson-Schumer report will be that cereal manufacturers have benefited more from the favorable publicity of cutting cereal prices than consumers have from lower prices, a Gedjenson aide said.
The report should be out in two to three weeks, he said.
